newsitem.title: FRANCE: French MPs propose cutting payments for abortions.
newsitem.headline: French MPs propose cutting payments for abortions.

text.p: A group of French parliamentarians proposed on Thursday to block the loss-making state welfare system from paying for abortions not required by the mother's health, parliamentary sources said.

Some 20 members of the ruling centre-right coalition tabled a bill saying that, "it is no longer appropriate to keep asking all citizens to fund...the reimbursement of medical procedures that are not intended to treat a disease".
France legalised abortion in 1975 and decided in 1982 that patients should be reimbursed by the state.
The government is currently seeking ways to rein in soaring medical costs as part of a drive to cut budget deficits in order to join the European single currency from 1999.
There was no immediate indication of when the proposal would come before the National Assembly.
Abortion is legal within 10 weeks after conception. Official figures show between 170,000 and 180,000 abortions -- one for every four births -- are performed every year.

Anti-abortion campaigners have become more militant over the past few years, staging sit-ins in hospitals where abortions are performed and lobbying for a tightening of the law, which pro-abortionists say is too strict.
The National Assembly last March overwhelmingly defeated a proposal that would have allowed abortion foes to press civil lawsuits against "incitements to abortion".

On the 20th anniversary of the legalisation of abortion last year, the government announced plans to give higher pay and better job security to doctors worried by a shortage of funds and attacks by anti-abortionists.
